worked.title: Q1 · Quartic minima and GD start; PCA direction; KKT at a given point (10 marks)

problem.text: (a) f(x) = 3x⁴ − 20x³ + 36x² + 10. (i) Stationary points, classify them, global minimum. [3M] (ii) Is x = 0.5 or x = 3.5 the better start for plain GD to reach the global minimum? [1M]  (b) X = [[2, −1, −2, 1], [−4, 2, 4, −2]] (columns are points). Student 1 says the direction of maximum variance is (1, 0), Student 2 says (0, 1), Student 3 says both are wrong. Find it. [2M]  (c) M = {(x, y): x² + y² ≤ 5, x + 2y = 4, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0}. (i) Formulate: point of M nearest the origin. [1M] (ii) Lagrangian. [1M] (iii) Multipliers so that (4/5, 8/5) satisfies KKT. [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (a) second-derivative test and where GD rolls to [4M]. (b) PC1 = top eigenvector of the covariance [2M]. (c) formulate, Lagrangian, KKT check [4M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: in (c) α₁, α₂, α₃ = inequality multipliers (λ on the boards), γ = equality multiplier (μ on the boards).

steps.label: (a)(i) STEP 3 · Global minimum  [0.5M]
steps.text:
f(0) = 10, f(3) = 243 − 540 + 324 + 10 = 37
**x = 0 is the global minimum** (f = 10); x = 3 is only a local minimum.

steps.label: (a)(ii) STEP 4 · Better start  [1M]
steps.text:
f′(0.5) = 12(0.5)(−1.5)(−2.5) = 22.5 > 0 ⇒ GD moves left, towards 0 ✓
f′(3.5) = 12(3.5)(1.5)(0.5) = 31.5 > 0 ⇒ GD moves left, towards 3, and the hill at 2 stops it there ✗
**x = 0.5** is better.

steps.label: (b) STEP 5 · Covariance
steps.text: Mean of each row = 0, so S = XXᵀ/4 = [[2.5, −5], [−5, 10]]

steps.label: (b) STEP 6 · Top eigenvector  [2M]
steps.text:
|S − λI| = λ² − 12.5λ = 0 ⇒ λ = 0, 12.5 [0.5M]
(S − 12.5I)v = 0: −10v₁ − 5v₂ = 0 ⇒ v₂ = −2v₁
v = (1, −2)/√5 (any multiple)
All four points lie on the line x₂ = −2x₁, so this is the only direction with variance.
**Student 3 is right** [1.5M].

steps.label: (c) STEP 7 · Formulate and Lagrangian  [2M]
steps.text:
min (x² + y²)^½ s.t. x² + y² − 5 ≤ 0, x + 2y − 4 = 0, −x ≤ 0, −y ≤ 0 [1M]
L = (x² + y²)^½ + α₁(x² + y² − 5) − α₂x − α₃y + γ(x + 2y − 4) [1M]

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) 0, 3 minima, 2 maximum; global min x = 0; start at 0.5. (b) v = (1, −2)/√5: Student 3. (c) (α₁, α₂, α₃, γ) = (0, 0, 0, −1/√5).

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (a) Calling x = 3 the global minimum without comparing f values.
• (b) Picking the eigenvector of the smaller eigenvalue.
• (c) Not checking that both stationarity equations give the same γ.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (c) in full: [Lecture 11, Lagrangian tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-lagrange/13).

worked.answer: (a) Global min at 0; start at 0.5. (b) (1, −2)/√5: Student 3. (c) α = 0, γ = −1/√5.
worked.priorityWhy: Older paper (2022–2023): its question types are covered in the lectures

worked.title: Q2 · Rank, dimension, span, RREF, eigenvalues: five short proofs (10 marks)

problem.text: (i) Rank of the n × n matrix with entries a_jk = j + k − 1. Does it change for a_jk = j + k − α (α a positive integer)? [2M]  (ii) Prove or disprove: the dimension of a vector space does not depend on its field. [2M]  (iii) If v₁ + v₂ + v₃ = 0, prove {v₁, v₂} and {v₂, v₃} span the same subspace. [2M]  (iv) A and B get the same RREF X̃ of X. C: impossible. D: possible. E: possible, and X can be recovered from X̃ if no entry of X is 0. Who is right? [2M]  (v) Given distinct eigenvalues λ₁, …, λₙ, can you build an orthogonal matrix of order n? [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Short justifications on rank, span, RREF and eigenvectors. 2 marks each.

steps.label: (i) STEP 1 · Rank  [2M]
steps.text:
Row j = (j, j + 1, …, j + n − 1) = j·(1, 1, …, 1) + (0, 1, …, n − 1)
Every row is a combination of the same two vectors ⇒ rank ≤ 2; rows 1 and 2 are not multiples ⇒ **rank 2** (n ≥ 2).
With −α instead of −1 the rows are (j + 1 − α)(1, …, 1) + (0, 1, …, n − 1): still **rank 2**. (Key: column 2 is a combination of columns 1 and 3.)

steps.label: (ii) STEP 2 · Dimension depends on the field  [2M]
steps.text: **False.** ℂ over ℝ: basis {1, i}, dimension 2. ℂ over ℂ: basis {1}, dimension 1.

steps.label: (iii) STEP 3 · Same span  [2M]
steps.text:
v₁ = −v₂ − v₃ [1M]
Any a v₁ + b v₂ = a(−v₂ − v₃) + b v₂ = (b − a)v₂ − a v₃ ∈ span{v₂, v₃}; the reverse is the same with v₃ = −v₁ − v₂ [1M] ⇒ equal spans.

steps.label: (iv) STEP 4 · RREF  [2M]
steps.text:
The RREF of a matrix is **unique** ⇒ A and B must agree: **D is right, C is wrong** [1M].
**E is wrong**: many matrices share one RREF, e.g. [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and [[2, 1], [1, 3]] both reduce to I, so X cannot be recovered from X̃ [1M].

steps.label: (v) STEP 5 · Orthogonal matrix  [2M]
steps.text:
**Yes.** Distinct eigenvalues ⇒ the eigenvectors of any B = PΛP⁻¹ (Λ = diag(λᵢ)) are independent [1M]; Gram–Schmidt turns them into an orthonormal set, i.e. an orthogonal matrix Q [1M].
(Simplest: take B = QΛQᵀ for any orthogonal Q; it is symmetric with exactly these eigenvalues.)

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (i) 2 in both cases. (ii) False (ℂ over ℝ vs ℂ). (iii) v₁ = −v₂ − v₃. (iv) D right; C and E wrong. (v) Yes, via Gram–Schmidt.

worked.answer: (i) Rank 2 both times. (ii) False. (iii) Proved. (iv) Only D. (v) Yes.
worked.priorityWhy: Older paper (2022–2023): its question types are covered in the lectures

worked.title: Q3 · ℓ₁ distance; convex solution set; eigenvalues of XXᵀ via XᵀX; exact line search (10 marks)

problem.text: (1)(i) Prove or disprove that d(x, y) = Σ|xᵢ − yᵢ| is a distance. [2M] (ii) Is C = {x | Ax = b} convex? [1M]  (2) x₁, …, x₂₀ ∈ ℝ¹⁰²⁴, S = Σxᵢxᵢᵀ (1024 × 1024). eig() only works below 32 rows. (a) Eigenvalues of S? [1.5M] (b) Eigenvectors? [1.5M]  (3) g(z) = ½‖Az − b‖² + ½‖z‖² + ‖b‖², A symmetric positive definite. (a) For z_{k+1} = z_k + αd_k, derive d_k (gradient descent). [2M] (b) Closed form for the optimal α = argmin g(z_k + αd_k). [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (1) metric axioms and the convex-set definition [3M]. (2) the XᵀX trick from PCA [3M]. (3) gradient and exact line search on a quadratic [4M].

steps.label: (1)(i) STEP 1 · Distance  [2M]
steps.text:
Non-negative, and 0 only when every xᵢ = yᵢ, i.e. x = y [0.5M]
Symmetric: |xᵢ − yᵢ| = |yᵢ − xᵢ| [0.5M]
Triangle: |xᵢ − yᵢ| ≤ |xᵢ − zᵢ| + |zᵢ − yᵢ|, add over i ⇒ d(x, y) ≤ d(x, z) + d(z, y) [1M]
**Yes, it is a distance.**

steps.label: (1)(ii) STEP 2 · Convex set  [1M]
steps.text: Az₁ = Az₂ = b ⇒ A(λz₁ + (1 − λ)z₂) = λb + (1 − λ)b = b ⇒ **convex**.

steps.label: (2) STEP 3 · Use the small matrix  [0.5M]
steps.text: S = XXᵀ with X = [x₁ … x₂₀] (1024 × 20). XᵀX is only **20 × 20**, so eig() can handle it.

steps.label: (2)(a) STEP 4 · Same eigenvalues  [1M]
steps.text:
If XᵀXc = λc, multiply by X: XXᵀ(Xc) = λ(Xc).
So every eigenvalue of XᵀX is an eigenvalue of S; the other 1004 eigenvalues of S are 0 (rank ≤ 20).

steps.label: (2)(b) STEP 5 · Eigenvectors  [1.5M]
steps.text: Run [P, D] = eig(XᵀX). For each column c of P: **d = Xc** is an eigenvector of S with the same λ (normalise d/‖d‖).

steps.label: (3)(a) STEP 6 · Gradient and d_k  [2M]
steps.text:
g = ½zᵀAᵀAz − zᵀAᵀb + ½bᵀb + ½zᵀz + bᵀb
∇g = AᵀAz − Aᵀb + z = (AᵀA + I)z − Aᵀb
**d_k = −∇g(z_k) = Aᵀb − (AᵀA + I)z_k**
⚠ The printed key writes ∇g with every sign flipped; the line above is the correct one.

steps.label: (3)(b) STEP 7 · Optimal step  [2M]
steps.text:
φ(α) = g(z_k + αd_k). g is quadratic, so
φ′(α) = ∇g(z_k + αd_k)ᵀd_k = (∇g(z_k) + α(AᵀA + I)d_k)ᵀd_k = −d_kᵀd_k + α d_kᵀ(AᵀA + I)d_k = 0
**α = d_kᵀd_k / (d_kᵀ(AᵀA + I)d_k) = ‖d_k‖² / (‖Ad_k‖² + ‖d_k‖²)**

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (1) Yes, a distance; C convex. (2) eig(XᵀX): same nonzero λ, eigenvectors Xc. (3) d_k = Aᵀb − (AᵀA + I)z_k; α = ‖d_k‖²/(‖Ad_k‖² + ‖d_k‖²).

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (2) Saying the eigenvalues are "approximately" equal: they are exactly equal (nonzero ones).
• (3) Copying the key's sign slip in ∇g.
• (3) Forgetting the +z from ½‖z‖².

steps.label: More
steps.text: (1)(ii) in full: [Lecture 11, Convexity tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-convex/20).

worked.answer: (1) Distance ✓, C convex. (2) Use XᵀX (20 × 20): same λ, eigenvectors Xc. (3) d_k = −∇g(z_k), α = ‖d_k‖²/(‖Ad_k‖² + ‖d_k‖²).

worked.title: Q4 · GD on a parabola in closed form; feature map of a kernel sum (10 marks)

problem.text: (1) f(x) = ax² + bx + c, a > 0, gradient descent with step λ. Can x_{n+k} be written as x_nP^k + Q? Find P and Q. For which λ does GD surely converge? [5M]  (2) K(x, z) = (xᵀz)² + 3(xᵀz + 2)². Find φ into ℝ^{n²+n+1} with K = φ(x)ᵀφ(z), or explain why not. [5M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (1) the GD multiplier r = 1 − λf″ on a parabola [5M]. (2) building a feature map by expanding the kernel [5M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's **λ is the step size** (η on the boards), not a multiplier. f″ = 2a.

steps.label: (1) STEP 1 · One step
steps.text:
x_{n+1} = x_n − λ(2ax_n + b) = (1 − 2aλ)x_n − λb
So **P = 1 − 2aλ**

steps.label: (1) STEP 2 · k steps  [2M]
steps.text:
x_{n+k} = P^k x_n − λb(1 + P + … + P^{k−1}) = P^k x_n − λb(1 − P^k)/(1 − P)
1 − P = 2aλ ⇒ **Q = −(b/2a)(1 − P^k)**
(Q depends on k but not on n; the key accepts this form.)
Neat form: x_{n+k} + b/2a = P^k (x_n + b/2a): the distance to the minimum −b/2a is multiplied by P each step.

steps.label: (1) STEP 3 · Convergence  [3M]
steps.text:
P^k → 0 needs |1 − 2aλ| < 1 ⇒ **0 < λ < 1/a**
Then x → −λb/(1 − P) = **−b/2a**, the minimum.
(Same rule as the boards: r = 1 − ηf″ with f″ = 2a; monotone below 1/(2a), oscillating between 1/(2a) and 1/a.)

steps.label: (2) STEP 4 · Expand  [2M]
steps.text: K = (xᵀz)² + 3[(xᵀz)² + 4xᵀz + 4] = **4(xᵀz)² + 12xᵀz + 12**

steps.label: (2) STEP 5 · Match each term  [3M]
steps.text:
4(xᵀz)² = ΣᵢΣⱼ (2xᵢxⱼ)(2zᵢzⱼ) ⇒ n² features 2xᵢxⱼ
12xᵀz = Σᵢ (√12 xᵢ)(√12 zᵢ) ⇒ n features √12 xᵢ
12 = √12 · √12 ⇒ 1 feature √12
**φ(x) = [2xᵢxⱼ (all i, j), √12 xᵢ, √12]**, length n² + n + 1 ✓

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (1) P = 1 − 2aλ, Q = −(b/2a)(1 − P^k); converges for 0 < λ < 1/a to −b/2a. (2) φ = [2xᵢxⱼ, √12 xᵢ, √12].

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (1) Writing the condition as λ < 1/(2a): that is only the no-oscillation limit.
• (2) Forgetting to expand 3(xᵀz + 2)² fully (the 12 and the 12xᵀz).

steps.label: More
steps.text: (1) background: [Lecture 9, step-size behaviour](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch09/lesson/9). (2) in full: [Lecture 14, Kernels tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch14/f-kernels/4).

worked.answer: (1) P = 1 − 2aλ, 0 < λ < 1/a. (2) φ(x) = [2xᵢxⱼ, √12 xᵢ, √12], dimension n² + n + 1.
worked.priorityWhy: Its kernel part (2) was asked again in Sep 2024
